labels.text: Picks the best model for each message

S79.01.note: The routing itself runs on the server; the side panel shows only the result.
steps: Sign in to the AGI Chrome side panel.
Look at the button under the message box; it reads "Auto" when Auto is selected.
Click that button and read the first row, "Auto", with its line "Picks the best model for each message".
Send a short chat question, then a coding question.
Look under each answer for a small line with a model name; compare it with Expected: Auto picks a model per request.
S79.01.where: Composer model button (reads "Auto" by default) > first row "Auto" in the menu

S79.02.note: Models the plan does not include show a lock instead of being selectable.
steps: Sign in and open the composer model button.
Under "Recommended", click a model name.
Confirm the composer button now shows that model instead of "Auto".
Send a message and read the model name under the answer.
Compare with Expected: the answer comes from the model you picked.
S79.02.where: Composer model button > "Recommended" list > click a model name, or "All models ($COUNT$)" for the full list

S79.04.note: The task-to-profile map is in packages/ai/model-registry/catalog/routing-policies.json (autoProfileByTask). The premium profile has no menu row of its own (auto-premium is not selectable), so it is seen only through the answering model.
steps: With "Auto" selected, send a plain chat question, then a coding request.
Read the model name under each answer.
Compare with Expected: coding and reasoning requests get the premium profile.
S79.04.where: Task profiles are set in the model registry; the effect shows as which model answers under Auto

labels.text: Answers faster on a cheaper route, good for summaries and quick lookups

S79.07.needs: a signed-in account whose plan includes the cheapest Auto route (the toggle is greyed out otherwise)
S79.07.note: The toggle is only enabled while Auto is selected. The UI wording says "cheaper route", weaker than Expected's "cheapest eligible route".
steps: Sign in and select "Auto" in the composer model button.
Open the model button and scroll to the "Quick" toggle, with its line "Answers faster on a cheaper route, good for summaries and quick lookups".
Switch "Quick" on and send a short question.
Read the model name under the answer and compare with the same question with "Quick" off.
Compare with Expected: Quick uses the cheaper route.
S79.07.where: Composer model button (with "Auto" selected) > "Quick" toggle below the "Effort" section

S79.09.note: Classification runs on the server (packages/ai/routing/src/classify.ts). Not visible directly.
steps: With "Auto" selected, send a greeting, then a request to write code.
Read the model name under each answer.
Compare with Expected: each request is routed by its task.
S79.09.where: Effect shows as a change of answering model between kinds of request

S79.10.note: The tool classification code cited (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts) is outside apps/extension, so it was not confirmed in the extension.
steps: With "Auto" selected, ask for information that needs a live web search.
Read the model name under the answer and check whether it names sources.
Open the model button > "All models ($COUNT$)" and use the "Web search" filter to see which models offer that capability.
Compare with Expected: the request is routed to a search-capable model.
S79.10.where: Effect shows as the answering model when a request needs tools; the capability names are in the model menu under "All models ($COUNT$)"

S79.11.needs: a file to upload (an image) and a signed-in account
S79.11.note: The attach menu item is in apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts; the trigger button's visible text was not confirmed.
steps: With "Auto" selected, open the composer attach menu and choose "Upload from device".
Pick an image and ask a question about it.
Read the model name under the answer; open the model button > "All models ($COUNT$)" and filter by "Vision" to see which models accept images.
Compare with Expected: the answer comes from a model that can read images.
S79.11.where: Effect shows when an image is attached; attach menu > "Upload from device"

S79.12.note: The classification is inner logic in packages/ai/routing/src/task-family.ts. The effort badge only shows once a model is resolved.
steps: With "Auto" selected, send a simple question and read the effort badge on the composer model button.
Send a hard multi-step problem and read the badge again.
Compare with Expected: the effort level changes with complexity.
S79.12.where: Effect shows in the composer model button's effort badge while Auto is selected

S79.13.note: Freshness detection is in apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts, outside apps/extension.
steps: With "Auto" selected, ask a question about today's news.
Check whether the answer names sources or links.
Open the model button > "All models ($COUNT$)" and use the "Web search" filter to compare capable models.
Compare with Expected: a freshness request goes to search-capable handling.
S79.13.where: Effect shows when the question needs current information; answer carries sources

S79.14.needs: a Free account, and a paid account to compare
S79.14.note: Filtering by capability, lifecycle, region and credentials runs in code; the tester sees only the resulting list.
steps: Sign in and open the composer model button.
Click "All models ($COUNT$)" and scroll the list.
Look for rows with a lock label and the hint "Opens plans in a new tab".
Pick an unlocked model and send a message to confirm it is used.
Compare with Expected: only models the plan allows can be chosen.

S79.15.note: The answer footer shows the model, not the provider route, so the health, cost and cache ranking cannot be seen from the UI. Ranking is in packages/ai/routing/src/auto.ts.
S79.15.where: Provider route is not shown; only the model name appears under each answer

S79.16.note: apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/managedModelPicker.ts reconcileManagedModelSelection drops a chosen model back to "auto" when the plan no longer lists it, which may be a silent switch to Auto.
steps: Pick a specific model from the composer model button.
Send several messages, including a hard one, in the same chat.
Read the model name under each answer and check that no "Moved to" line appears.
Compare with Expected: the chosen model is never swapped.
S79.16.where: Composer model button > pick a model under "Recommended" or "All models ($COUNT$)"

S79.19.note: Quota-aware choice is in apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts. No visible effect could be confirmed from the extension UI.
S79.19.where: Server rule on routing; no visible meter in the side panel

S79.20.needs: a signed-in account; a route outage cannot be forced from the UI
S79.20.note: Health fallback is in apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts and route.ts. The reason phrase for it is in packages/contracts/types/src/auto-route-explanation.ts.
steps: With "Auto" selected, send several messages in one chat.
Look under each answer for a line starting "Moved to" and read its reason.
Compare with Expected: an unhealthy route is replaced by a healthy one.
S79.20.where: Effect shows as a "Moved to" line under an answer when Auto avoids a model with trouble

S79.26.needs: a signed-in account; the "Moved to" line appears only when the model changes
S79.26.note: The line only appears when Auto actually moves to another model; forcing one may need a longer chat.
steps: Sign in with "Auto" selected.
Send messages until Auto answers with a different model; a line reading "Moved to ..." appears under that answer.
Read the reason after the colon.
Hover the model name in the answer footer and read the tooltip "Auto chose this model: ...".
Compare with Expected: the user can see why Auto chose or moved to a model.
S79.26.where: Chat answer > "Moved to" line under the answer; hover the model name in the answer footer

S79.27.note: The footer is built in apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/bubbles.ts (answerMetaLabel) and has no fixed visible words of its own.
steps: Sign in and send a message.
Read the small line under the answer: a model name, then a time.
Open the composer model button and compare the name with the model you chose.
Compare with Expected: each answer names the model that produced it.
S79.27.where: Answer footer under each reply (model name · duration)

S79.30.note: Fallback on ambiguous classification is in packages/ai/routing/src/task-family.ts and the classification code; no visible control or message for it was found in the extension.
S79.30.where: Effect shows as an answer that still arrives with a named model when routing is unsure
